data.narrative:
Cartesia is a Series B AI & Software company founded by Karan Goel, Albert Gu, Arjun Desai, Brandon Yang, and Chris Ré, having raised $186M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 private same-stage, same-sector comparables—Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B)—alongside 1 public comp (Palantir) and 7 additional private frontier-AI firms.

Two valuation methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier to the $186M raised, implying a valuation of $353M. This method assumes typical Series B advancement mechanics but may underweight the target's positioning within the frontier-AI cohort. The peer-median approach uses the 3-company median of $3.2B, spanning a range of $2.0B to $5.6B, and reflects current market pricing for AI infrastructure and model development at this stage. These methods diverge significantly, reflecting both methodological sensitivity and heterogeneity in peer-stage valuations.

Triangulation across both methods yields a range of $300M (low bound, stage-progression discount) to $3.7B (high bound, near peer-max). The median implied value of $1.8B sits materially below peer-median, suggesting either a discount for capital efficiency or uncertainty around differentiated capability. Key uncertainties include the specificity of peer comparability and whether $186M in cumulative raise reflects pre-Series B or post-Series B capital.
